rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

cashPosition.reason: Saturday, US equities closed. Spot-crypto-only universe. No dated weekend catalyst; every liquid spot pair carries a ~1.9% round-trip spread that exceeds the realistic 24h move. Pre-committed cash default from the 2026-09-18 run.
cashPosition.catalyst: SATURDAY 2026-09-19 -- US EQUITY MARKETS ARE CLOSED, SPOT CRYPTO IS THE ONLY PERMITTED UNIVERSE, AND I AM TAKING NO POSITION. THE BOOK IS 100% CASH AT $9,429.09. This is not indecision. It is pre-commitment (1) from yesterday's run executing exactly as written, and I am recording the whole chain so it cannot later be re-described as a hunch. Yesterday I wrote, before I knew today's tape: 'TOMORROW IS SATURDAY 2026-09-19 AND US EQUITY MARKETS ARE CLOSED, SO THE SPOT-CRYPTO-ONLY RULE BINDS... Given the 1.9% round-trip spread I measured today, the weekend position must clear a materially higher bar than a weekday one, and 100% CASH IS THE DEFAULT for Saturday unless a spot-crypto candidate has a genuine dated catalyst inside the weekend -- "crypto is strong" does not qualify and I have now written down why.' I searched for a dated weekend catalyst. There is none I can own. So the default stands. CLOSED SSO AT 69.39 FOR -$32.61 (-0.34%). Entry was 69.63, Friday's canonical settle is 69.39, and THE LOSS IS ENTIRELY THE ENTRY GAP -- which is the single risk I named loudest, two days running. SSO rose on the session: 69.29 settle on 9/17 to 69.39 on 9/18, +0.14%, and SPY rose +0.12% on a dividend-adjusted basis (761.64 against an adjusted 760.71 after Friday's ex-div; the unadjusted 762.60 print overstates the decline). The index went my way. I still lost, because I paid 69.63 for something that settled at 69.39. I bought a 0.49% pre-market premium and the market delivered 0.14%. On Thursday I wrote 'I AM BUYING A GAP AND GAPS FADE... If that happens I lose the 1.12% on the entry alone before any thesis is tested. This is the single most likely way today goes wrong.' On Friday I told myself the gap argument no longer applied because SPY was +0.02% and therefore SSO's half-point of premium was 'a normal pre-market mark, not a crowd paying up.' THAT WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS WRONG IN A SPECIFIC, LEARNABLE WAY: a 2x fund's pre-market print carries its own premium independent of the index's, and I treated 2x of a two-basis-point move as though it explained 49 basis points. It does not. It explains four. The other 45 were the premium I claimed I was not paying. PRE-COMMITMENT (3) FIRES: THE CAP RETURNS TO 1x FOR MONDAY. I wrote 'If SSO closes RED, the cap returns to 1x immediately and I must write down whether the quad-witching argument was analysis or rationalisation.' SSO closed red against my entry. Here is the answer, and it is uncomfortable: THE QUAD-WITCHING ARGUMENT WAS RATIONALISATION WEARING THE CLOTHES OF ANALYSIS. My actual decision was made by the stop-cover screen, which returned exactly one eligible instrument out of four. SSO was not chosen; it was the residue. The quad-witching paragraph -- 'own the DEEPEST, most arbitraged, most liquid exposure available' -- was written AFTER the screen had already decided, to make a forced outcome look elective. The tell is that I argued both sides in the same file: the risks section then said 'I may have chosen precisely the instrument most exposed to the day's dominant mechanical force while telling myself it was the safest.' A genuine analysis does not need to be hedged against itself in the adjacent paragraph. The honest framing of Friday's trade was: my rules left me one instrument and I took it. PRE-COMMITMENT (4) RESOLVED, INSIDE ITS BAND. I wrote 'If QLD outperforms SSO by more than 1.5% today, I must NOT conclude the 1.21x rejection was wrong.' QLD went 89.94 -> 91.02, +1.20%. SSO went 69.29 -> 69.41 (RTH last), +0.17%. Outperformance 1.03%, inside the 1.5% threshold. The clause did not even need to protect me. But the instruments I barred on the 2x CAP rather than the stop test are a different and much louder story, and I am publishing the numbers rather than omitting them: SOXL 114.82 -> 123.77, +7.80%. BITX 16.64 -> 18.69, +12.32%. NVDL 34.04 -> 34.86, +2.41%. THE LEVERAGE CAP COST THIS BOOK 7.8% AND 12.3% ON FRIDAY, ON THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE MORNING SOXL LED THE BOARD. That is the price of the streak rule and I should look straight at it rather than filing it under 'process worked.' The defence is real -- a rule that only binds when it is cheap is not a rule, and BITX's 1.02x stop cover was decorative whatever it returned -- but $9,429 of capital does not care about the defence. I am not changing the rule on the day after it hurt. I am writing the number down so that when I DO review it (pre-commitment 5, due Monday) I am reviewing it against evidence and not against a feeling. TODAY'S TAPE -- AND WHY A GOOD-LOOKING CRYPTO BID IS STILL NOT A TRADE. Friday was a big crypto day: BTC +5.8% on the session per Motley Fool, driven by four things I can name -- the SEC granting a five-year exemption for limited on-chain trading of tokenised stocks, oil retreating as the Saudi East-West pipeline restoration continued, US spot BTC ETFs taking $433M of net inflows on 9/18 alone (FBTC +$311M, IBIT +$108M) and $591M over two days, and roughly $603.39M of short liquidations across 119,948 traders. CoinDesk has 98 of the CoinDesk 100 advancing with Starknet and Arbitrum +17%, and the 10-year back below 5%. EVERY ONE OF THOSE FOUR CATALYSTS ALREADY FIRED. They are Friday facts, and I am being asked to buy them on Saturday morning. The overnight tape says the same thing: against the midnight-CT boundary, BTC mark 81,216.80 vs 81,017.12 open = +0.25%, ETH 2,642.18 vs 2,619.06 = +0.88%, SOL 111.95 vs 112.34 = -0.35%, DOGE +0.42%, XRP +0.41%, LTC 57.31 vs 58.19 = -1.50%. The complex is FLAT-TO-MIXED. The move is over; what is left is the price it finished at. THE DECISIVE ARITHMETIC IS THE ONE I MEASURED YESTERDAY AND IT IS WORSE THIS MORNING, NOT BETTER. Robinhood market-maker-routed quotes at 05:40:17 CT: BTC 80,456.92 / 81,976.68 = 1.87% quoted spread. ETH 2,617.29 / 2,667.07 = 1.88%. SOL 110.89 / 113.01 = 1.90%. DOGE 0.08694956 / 0.08862014 = 1.90%. XRP 1.40680 / 1.43383 = 1.90%. LTC 56.764 / 57.865 = 1.92%. I buy the ask and sell the bid, so a 24-hour round trip starts ~1.9% down. FOR ME TO BREAK EVEN BY TOMORROW MORNING, BITCOIN MUST RISE 1.9% ON A SATURDAY, THE DAY AFTER IT ROSE 5.8%, WITH THE ETF BID STRUCTURALLY ABSENT. Spot bitcoin ETFs do not trade on Saturday. The $433M that drove Friday cannot arrive during any part of my holding period. The $603M of forced short-covering is spent -- liquidations are fuel that burns once. So I would be paying a 1.9% toll to hold an asset whose two identified marginal buyers are both switched off for the entire duration of the position. cashPosition.driver: 100% CASH -- NO POSITION. $9,429.09 undeployed. Zero shares, zero exposure, zero fees, zero spread paid. THE POSITIVE CASE FOR CASH, STATED AS A TRADE RATHER THAN AS A FAILURE TO FIND ONE. On a weekday I can express a 1% view for 1.4 basis points of spread (SSO quoted 69.62/69.63 yesterday). On a Saturday the cheapest instrument in my permitted universe costs 187 basis points. That is a 130-fold increase in the price of having an opinion, and my opinion has not become 130 times better. The expected 24h move in spot BTC is on the order of 1.5-2.5%; the guaranteed cost is 1.87%. Directionally I would need to be right AND right by more than the toll, which means I need roughly a 60-65% hit rate just to break even on a coin flip that I have no dated information about. CASH HAS A HIGHER EXPECTED VALUE THAN ANY AVAILABLE TRADE TODAY, and that is a position, not an abstention. CANDIDATES SCANNED AND WHY EACH FAILS. (a) SPOT BTC at 81,976.68 ask -- the momentum trade and the one I had to argue myself out of. Rejected on three grounds that compound: the catalyst is spent (SEC tokenised-stock exemption, oil retreat, ETF inflows and $603M of short liquidations are all Friday events, and the tape confirms it -- +0.25% overnight after +5.8% on the day); the marginal buyer is structurally absent, because spot BTC ETFs are closed all weekend and the $433M that drove Friday cannot arrive inside my window; and the 1.87% round trip exceeds the realistic move. Buying a finished move at a 1.9% toll with the buyer switched off is the closest thing to a negative-expectancy trade on this board. (b) SPOT ETH at 2,667.07 -- the best 24h performer of the majors at +0.88% and the only one with a structural weekend bid (staking, exchange balances). Rejected because +0.88% overnight is under half the 1.88% spread, so it is already a losing position at entry, and because the Glamsterdam fork that would justify owning ETH specifically is a TESTNET event, provisional, and lands Monday -- after my exit. I bought ETH on this exact weekend logic on 9/12 and lost 2.11%; the lesson then was that a single-observation relative-strength signal is not a catalyst, and +0.88% is a single observation. (c) SPOT SOL at 113.01 -- negative overnight (-0.35%) and the highest-beta major, so it is the worst combination available: paying the widest effective cost to own the asset with the most downside and no catalyst. (d) DOGE, XRP, LTC -- scanned for completeness and to make sure I was not confining myself to the majors out of habit. All three carry the same ~1.9% spread with none of BTC's depth; LTC is the worst-performing liquid pair on the board at -1.50%. No dated events. Rejected. (e) LAYERZERO / ZRO short -- the one genuinely dated, genuinely asymmetric weekend event I found: 25.71M tokens, >7% of market cap, unlocking Sunday 9/20 into a thin weekend book. It is the correct trade and I cannot take it. This book is long-only in spot, ZRO is not a Robinhood spot pair, and there is no inverse wrapper that trades on a Saturday. Naming it explicitly because 'I found no catalyst' would be false -- I found one, it pointed down, and the instrument does not exist for me. (f) LEVERAGED CRYPTO ETFs -- BITX, T-REX 2X Inverse Bitcoin, Volatility Shares 2X Solana. All equity-listed, all closed Saturday, all barred by mandate regardless of how good BITX's Friday (+12.32%) looked. (g) ALL EQUITIES AND EQUITY ETFs -- SOXL, SSO, QLD, NVDL, SPXL, TQQQ and the rest -- markets closed, barred by mandate. Verified: NYSE and Nasdaq observe no Saturday session; the next open is Monday 2026-09-21. WHY I AM NOT SPLITTING THE DIFFERENCE. The tempting compromise on a day like this is a small or 'defensive' position -- park in BTC because it is the lowest-variance thing available, as I did on Sunday 9/13 (bought at 76,711.53, sold at 77,934.05, +$162.62). That trade worked. It worked because BTC was the best 24h performer AND the lowest-variance asset simultaneously, which is a genuine, if modest, edge. Today BTC is +0.25% overnight after a 5.8% day -- it is neither the strongest nor structurally supported, and the 9/13 entry did not face a spent catalyst. More importantly, this book's mandate is 100% or nothing; there is no 'small' here. A position today is an all-in bet on a coin flip with a 1.9% handicap. I have lost $570.91 from inception and the way that number gets worse is by paying tolls for opinions I do not have. THE PRECEDENT I AM DELIBERATELY SETTING. This is the first day in this book's history that I have chosen cash. On 9/12 and 9/13 -- both weekend days with, by my own contemporaneous notes, 'no catalyst inside the 24h window' and 'genuinely low-edge' -- I traded anyway, and I named cash as the runner-up both times. Those two trades netted -$57.55 combined (-$220.17 on ETH, +$162.62 on BTC) plus two round trips of spread I did not then measure. I have now measured the spread, written the number down, pre-committed to a cash default in advance of seeing the tape, and followed it. The rule was written yesterday by a version of me who did not know what today's prices would be, which is precisely the version that should be deciding this.
cashPosition.risks: THE PRIMARY RISK IS OBVIOUS AND I SHOULD NOT DRESS IT UP: CRYPTO RUNS THIS WEEKEND AND I OWN NONE OF IT. BTC just took out $80,000 on genuine regulatory news and real institutional flow, 98 of the CoinDesk 100 advanced, layer-2s are up 17%, and momentum regimes in crypto persist through weekends more often than they reverse. If BTC adds another 3-4% by tomorrow morning I will have watched roughly $300 of opportunity go past while sitting in cash, on a book that is down $570.91 and needs the money. That is a real cost with a real number attached, and 'the spread made it negative-expectancy' will be cold comfort. THE DEEPER CRITICISM: MY SPREAD ARGUMENT PROVES TOO MUCH, AND IF I BELIEVE IT I HAVE JUST BANNED MYSELF FROM EVERY WEEKEND FOREVER. The 1.9% round trip is not a feature of today. It is a permanent feature of Robinhood's market-maker crypto book. If a 1.9% toll disqualifies a 24-hour spot position, then it disqualifies EVERY Saturday and EVERY Sunday position this book will ever consider, which means roughly 29% of my trading days are now structurally cash -- and I have reached that sweeping conclusion over two days, from one measurement, without ever testing it against realised weekend moves. The honest version of the test is a distribution, not a threshold: what fraction of Saturday-to-Sunday BTC moves exceed 1.9% in absolute terms? If it is 40-50%, then the toll is a handicap I can sometimes overcome with a real edge, not an absolute bar, and today's reasoning is too blunt. I have not run that number. I should, and I am adding it to Monday's review rather than pretending today's argument is more rigorous than it is. A SECOND CRITICISM, AND I THINK IT IS THE SHARPEST ONE AVAILABLE AGAINST ME TODAY: CASH IS THE MOST COMFORTABLE POSSIBLE ANSWER FOR A BOOK THAT HAS JUST LOST MONEY FOUR TIMES IN SIX SESSIONS, AND COMFORT IS EXACTLY WHAT I SHOULD DISTRUST. I have lost on GUSH, TMV, UGL and now SSO; I won on QQQ and BTC. A losing streak produces a powerful pull toward doing nothing, and doing nothing can always be justified after the fact, because the costs of inaction never appear on a P&L line. Every argument I made above is one I could have made on 9/13, when I traded BTC and made $162.62. What actually changed is not the spread -- that was identical -- but the fact that I lost yesterday. I cannot fully rule out that the loss, not the analysis, is what made cash feel correct this morning. The strongest counter-evidence I can offer is that I wrote the cash default down YESTERDAY, before the SSO result was known and while I was still describing myself as having broken a losing streak. But I note that yesterday's me was also the one who had just lost three in a row, so the pre-commitment may carry the same contamination one day earlier. I cannot resolve this from the inside. I am flagging it so that if cash becomes a habit rather than a decision, the pattern is already on the record. A THIRD: I MAY BE OVERWEIGHTING 'THE CATALYST ALREADY FIRED.' Markets are not obliged to complete a repricing in one session. The SEC's five-year tokenised-stock exemption is a structural change to what can trade on-chain, not a one-day headline, and structural regulatory news typically reprices over weeks. The ETF inflow figure I cited ($591M over two days, accelerating into $433M on Friday) is a TREND, and trends that accelerate into a Friday frequently continue into the following Monday -- which means the weekend is where the position gets established cheaply, not where it gets avoided. My 'the buyer is switched off' point cuts the other way too: with ETFs closed, weekend price discovery happens in a thinner book, which amplifies moves in BOTH directions and is exactly the condition under which an asymmetric payoff -- this book's stated mandate -- is available. I have used weekend thinness as a reason to stay out; it is equally a reason a moonshot book exists at all. FOURTH, ON THE LOSS ITSELF: -0.34% IS A GOOD OUTCOME DISGUISED AS A BAD ONE, AND I SHOULD NOT LEARN THE WRONG LESSON FROM IT. The stop-cover screen delivered exactly what it promised -- the calmest instrument on the board produced the smallest loss this book has taken. Had I bought BITX at 1.02x cover I would be up 12.32%; had I bought it on a day it went the other way, a -7.86% session would have blown through the stop entirely. One observation of the counterfactual is not evidence about the screen. The screen's actual failure mode, which I named on Friday and repeat now, is that it selects for low volatility rather than for edge, and a book called Moonshot cannot run a filter whose binding constraint systematically eliminates asymmetry. That remains the thing to fix on Monday. FIFTH, A PROCESS RISK SPECIFIC TO TODAY: NO POSITION MEANS NO STOP, NO EXIT DISCIPLINE, AND NOTHING TO BE ACCOUNTABLE FOR TOMORROW. A cash day is the one day where I cannot be proven wrong by a price, which makes it the easiest day to write good-sounding prose. I have tried to guard against that by publishing the exact numbers that argue against me -- SOXL +7.80%, BITX +12.32%, NVDL +2.41%, and the fact that the leverage cap, not analysis, is what kept me out of them. THE MOTIVE CHECK, RUN EXPLICITLY. Evidence the process is real: the cash default was written down 24 hours in advance, in specific language, by a me who did not know today's prices; I searched for a weekend catalyst rather than assuming none existed, and I found one (the ZRO unlock) and reported it even though it pointed down and I could not trade it; I scanned six spot pairs including three outside the majors rather than stopping at BTC; I published the full cost of the rules that bound me (SOXL +7.8%, BITX +12.3%) rather than burying them; and I answered pre-commitment (3) against myself, conceding the quad-witching argument was rationalisation. Evidence for concern: cash is free of the possibility of being wrong, I have lost four of six, and I notice this is the first cash day in the book's history arriving immediately after a loss rather than during the three-loss streak when the case for stepping back was at least as strong. FOR THE NEXT RUN -- CONCRETE PRE-COMMITMENTS. (1) TOMORROW IS SUNDAY 2026-09-20, US EQUITIES CLOSED AGAIN, SPOT CRYPTO ONLY. The cash default carries forward BUT IT IS NOT AUTOMATIC: if BTC's Saturday-to-Sunday move exceeds 1.9% in EITHER direction, that is one live observation that the spread is survivable and I must say so in writing rather than quietly reusing today's argument. Two consecutive cash days is a policy, and a policy needs more justification than a decision. (2) IF BTC IS UP MORE THAN 3% BY TOMORROW'S RUN, I MUST NOT CHASE IT -- that is the same spent-catalyst-plus-toll setup one day later and 3% worse, and buying it would be pure regret-trading. I am recording this before I know the outcome, exactly as I did with SMH on Wednesday and QLD on Friday. (3) THE LEVERAGE CAP IS 1x FOR MONDAY by pre-commitment (3), which SSO's red close has now triggered. It does not reset because of a weekend and it does not reset because I was flat. If the answer is above ~45%, today's blanket reasoning was too blunt and I will say so. (5) I MUST NOT TREAT TODAY'S FLAT RESULT AS A WIN. Cash neither made nor lost money; it did not 'beat' anything. If BTC rises overnight, cash underperformed and I will record it as such in tomorrow's realised-outcome section. PRICING AND PROCEDURE.
